newsitem.title: UK: British Gas mulls bringing demerger forward.
newsitem.headline: British Gas mulls bringing demerger forward.

text.p: British Gas said it is studying whether its planned split-up, originally scheduled to happen in the spring of 1997, can take place earlier in the year.

A spokesman said the option is being considered simply because British Gas wants to have the demerger out of the way as soon possible, stressing there were no outside pressures to bring the break-up forward.
"The demerger is not connected to the other issues we are currently looking at," he said, referring to regulatory price reviews and British Gas' attempts to renegotiate contracts with gas producers.
"Any successful company -- when they have any proposals -- want to do them as quickly as they can," the spokesman said.
Troubled British Gas plans to split itself into a gas trading company, to be called British Gas Energy, and a transport firm called TransCo International.
The loss-making trading operations suffer from the famed take-or-pay contracts which oblige British Gas to buy gas from North Sea producers even it cannot find a market.

The pipeline operations meanwhile face the threat of lower profits due to harsh price proposals from industry watchdog Ofgas. The proposals are currently being vetted by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
British Gas said it was too early yet to indicate when a decision on the demerger's timing will be reached.
"There are a number of options and a number of issues to be sorted out first," the spokesman.
The Daily Telegraph newspaper said in a report on Friday that the company has called for a board meeting on November 8 to discuss a "fast track" break-up.
